long_biography.plain_text:
As an electrical-engineering student at the University of Waterloo, Lazaridis won a General Motors contract and left before graduating to build Research In Motion with Doug Fregin. The company moved from contract electronics and film-editing technology into wireless data, eventually creating the BlackBerry platform that made secure mobile email mainstream and generated Lazaridis's fortune.

His interest in the science behind computation then became an institutional project. Lazaridis founded Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, helped establish Waterloo's Institute for Quantum Computing and funded major research facilities. Through Quantum Valley Investments, which he co-founded with Fregin, he now combines technical guidance and capital to move quantum discoveries from laboratories towards commercial products and companies.
long_biography.html:
As an electrical-engineering student at the University of Waterloo, Lazaridis won a General Motors contract and left before graduating to build Research In Motion with Doug Fregin. The company moved from contract electronics and film-editing technology into wireless data, eventually creating the BlackBerry platform that made secure mobile email mainstream and generated Lazaridis's fortune.

His interest in the science behind computation then became an institutional project. Lazaridis founded Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, helped establish Waterloo's Institute for Quantum Computing and funded major research facilities. Through Quantum Valley Investments, which he co-founded with Fregin, he now combines technical guidance and capital to move quantum discoveries from laboratories towards commercial products and companies.
